blocchi: Radiology Quiz is a proof of concept (POC): a demonstration and experimental version of the platform, meant to test the idea with real users. Features and content may change, cases are under review, and the service may be interrupted or lose data.

Radiology Quiz is a training platform for physicians in radiology residency. Each case contains anonymized DICOM images to be read in a full-featured viewer, plus a guided quiz: exam technique, findings by anatomical region, and conclusion.
All images are anonymized: names, exact dates, healthcare facilities and physicians are removed before upload. Only the month and year of the exam are kept; age is the age at the time of the exam.

Artificial intelligence and software: the platform uses only open source software and artificial intelligence models, in order to improve physicians' training with sound, modern tools: TotalSegmentator (only the tasks with an Apache-2.0 license) for organ segmentation and automatic measurements in CT; the viewer is built on Cornerstone3D and vtk.js; in trial, report correction with Qwen3-4B (Apache-2.0) running in the browser with WebLLM. A model is used only if its code, weights and training data are all free. The models run offline on already anonymized cases, before publication: no image is sent to external services. AI suggestions are estimates to be verified; students see them after answering. Full list with authors and licenses: “Licenses and credits” page (licenze.html).

Report correction in the browser (experimental, if enabled by the administrator; authors and teachers can always try it): after answering, in the report box, “Correct the report”. An open source model (Qwen3-4B) runs on your computer with WebGPU (recent Chrome or Edge): the text never leaves your computer. The first time, the browser downloads the model (about 2.3 GB), which then stays in the cache. It gives a grade, the findings cited and missed, incorrect statements (only those you actually wrote) and a comment; it is a small model, so the assessment is indicative and does not change the case score. It is generated automatically and can be wrong: it is not saved or sent to the server, does not appear in the results your teacher sees and is not used to assess whoever writes the report. It is only feedback for practice.

📲 Install as app (home page): radio-quiz opens full screen from its icon, handy on a tablet. In Chrome and Edge the button uses the browser installation (or the menu: “Install radio-quiz”); on iPad and iPhone: Share → “Add to Home Screen”; in Safari on the Mac: File → “Add to Dock”.
Five steps for your first case:
1. In the case list press «Random practice» (or open a case from the list).
2. Read the history and the question: they are in the panel next to the images or, on small screens, below them (the «Answer ↓» button above the images takes you there).

3. Look at the images: mouse wheel or left-drag to scroll, right-drag for the window (brightness and contrast), double-click to enlarge a viewport. Series are in the thumbnail strip; hovering over a button shows what it does.

4. Answer one step at a time (for example Findings, then Conclusions): tick the answers you think are right and for each one say how sure you are (Certain, Probable or Hypothesis). Confidence does not change the score: in your statistics it shows whether you trust your reading too much or too little.
5. Press «Confirm answer»: you immediately see the correction, the discussion, the outcome and the images where the finding is best seen. Then «Next case».

The score is: right answers ticked minus wrong answers ticked, divided by the number of right answers in the case (all steps together). You can open this Help during a case too: it opens over the images and, when you close it, your answers are as you left them. If you leave a case before confirming, the platform asks first, because unconfirmed answers are lost.

Short videos (about one minute each, no voice, with Italian captions) that show the platform in use on a phone and the client viewer. They are on YouTube, in the playlist “Quiz Radiologia – Tutorial”: tap a video to open it. Until you open one, this page does not connect to YouTube.

blocchi.testo: From choosing a case to the correction: viewer, findings with your confidence level, diagnosis and discussion.
Scrolling through slices, lung, bone and mediastinum windows, zoom, measurements in millimetres and side-by-side series.
Axial, sagittal and coronal together, linked by a shared point, and a 3D volume you can rotate.
“Report only” mode, comparison with the expected report, “Show the finding”, progress and statistics.
Pathology slides from low to high magnification, measurements in micrometres, histological diagnosis.
The client viewer opens slides from the main scanners: the 12 sample slides, from Aperio SVS to Olympus VSI, from the whole slide to high magnification.
Create a challenge with 3 to 10 cases, choose how long it lasts and tag your friends: same cases for everyone, corrections at the end, leaderboard.

blocchi: Student: anyone who registers (medical and health profession students, residents, radiologists, physicians of other specialties, radiologic technologists). Students solve cases, track their own progress and choose their own reference teachers.

Teacher: a registered user who declares themselves a teacher, at registration or from the profile, with no need for approval. Teachers create classes and assign cases to those who chose them as reference, and see their results and progress.
Service administrator: uploads and corrects cases (the only manual part), decides which are visible and, if needed, intervenes on accounts.
Cases are common to everyone. A teacher sees only the results of those who chose them; each person can choose several teachers and remove them at any time.

From the login page, “Sign up”: first and last name, email, a password (at least 10 characters, with a number or a symbol), who you are (resident, radiologist, physician of another specialty…), and optionally your site. You receive an email with the link to activate the account: it is valid for 48 hours.
You log in with email and password. “Forgot password?” sends a link to choose a new one, valid for one hour. After five wrong passwords, login is locked for 15 minutes.

You can also sign in with “Continue with Google” or “Continue with LinkedIn”, without a password: the first time you complete your category, the terms of use and the 18+ declaration. If the Gmail address is already registered, Google enters the same account; otherwise sign in with your password and link Google or LinkedIn from your profile (“Sign in with Google and LinkedIn”).
Administrators and accounts created with a personal code log in with “Sign in with a code”. From the profile, these accounts too can enter an email and choose a password.
The “👤 Profile” button at the top opens your profile: data, reference teachers, email notifications, password and account deletion. The ◐ button switches between the dark and light theme.
Search: the box at the top searches by clinical suspicion, body region or title; suggestions appear as you type.
Modalities: the tabs filter by CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, mammography and nuclear medicine.

Difficulty: Basic, Intermediate or Advanced. When at least 5 users have answered a case, the difficulty is calculated from their average first-attempt score (≥75% Basic, 50-74% Intermediate, below 50% Advanced; ⓘ symbol); before that, the one set by the teacher applies. The menu next to the filters shows only cases of one difficulty.
Assigned tasks: the cases assigned by the teacher, with the due date and progress.

Home page in sections: Learning paths, Assignments and the cases of each modality (CT, MRI, X-ray…) open and close with a click on the title, which shows how many cases there are and how many you have completed; the browser remembers which ones you left open. With a search or a modality selected, the case sections open automatically.

Learning paths and Error review: sequences of cases by topic, sorted from the easiest path to the hardest and, within each path, from basic to advanced cases; the “Scales and classifications” path collects the cases in which a scale is filled in (BI-RADS, Bosniak, LI-RADS, Genant, Fazekas…). Review brings back the cases you got wrong after some days.
Random practice: one case after another, with no repetitions within the session.

⏱ Mock exam: cases picked at random from the current filter (area, modality, difficulty, search), with a total time (from 2 to 8 minutes per case). During the test the correction is not shown; when time runs out, the answers already chosen are submitted and unattempted cases score 0. At the end: average score, perfect cases, comparison with the average of registered users on the same cases (where there are at least 5 answers) and the correction of each case.
📍 Question on the figure: in cases with this symbol, in addition to the answers you indicate with a click the point on the image where the main finding is seen.

Custom path: after 10 completed cases, in the “Learning paths” section the platform suggests the cases you have not done yet in the areas (modality and region) where your average is below 70%, from the easiest, plus one case from areas you have never tried.

Level exam (⏱ Mock exam): Basic, Intermediate, Advanced or Mixed, always 10 cases from all modalities and 3 minutes per case, so that results can be compared over time. The history (first, last, best, trend) is on the same page and is also visible to your reference teacher.

The top bar contains all the commands as icons; hovering the mouse over an icon shows its name. Tools not suited to the modality do not appear (for example no RECIST or density in ultrasound, X-ray and mammography). When a case opens, if the teacher has not chosen the layout, the series arrange themselves by type of exam: in chest CT the lung on the left and the mediastinum on the right; in MRI up to four sequences of the same plane (T2, T1, diffusion, post-contrast).

The bar is divided into groups, from the left: Navigation (window, pan, zoom, magnifier, linked point, window presets), Measurements (ruler, RECIST, elliptical and freehand ROI, angle, arrow with annotation; in the ▾ menu profile, volume, Cobb, cardiothoracic ratio, “What structure is this?”), Image (rotate, flip, invert, sharpness, local contrast, cine, reset), Report (measurements in the report, Σ scales, ASPECTS, clear measurements; in the ••• menu breast density, vertebrae, anatomy quiz, radiomics) and Comparison (viewports, synchronization and coregistration, fusion, subtraction, comparison with the prior). The thick slab (MIP, MinIP, average) is next to Ax / Cor / Sag and applies only to the selected viewport. With the “Scroll images” tool the pointer is the arrow; clicking the active tool again turns it off and goes back to “Scroll”. At the top, as in the downloadable viewer: 📸 Key, 💾 Save (annotations), 📝 Report, ✕ Close (back to the case list) and ⋯ with “Multi-screen” (another window with the images only, for a second screen, following scrolling, window and zoom) and “link windows”. On narrow and touch screens only the icons remain. The ⋯ menu also has “📌 Remember” with “automatic layout”: when the case opens the screen arranges itself (the layout remembered for that exam type, mammography in 4 views, side-by-side phases), unless the teacher chose a layout for the case. Σ Scales proposes first the scales suited to the exam. If the active tool is in a menu, the menu button takes its icon. On wide screens the bar wraps instead of hiding icons; on the phone it scrolls sideways.

Window: drag to change level (up/down) and width (right/left). The window menu contains the CT presets; for X-rays the Bone, Soft tissue and High contrast presets, in mammography Calcifications, Dense breast, Skin and subcutaneous tissue (derived from the image values, which in X-ray and mammography are not HU).

X-rays: when opened, the window is calculated on the patient's values (excluding collimators and background) and local contrast is on; the histogram icon turns it off and on again. Local contrast (adaptive equalization) makes very bright and very dark areas readable together, for example thoracic and lumbar spine on the same film. Measurements and ROIs remain on the original values.

Tablet: one finger scrolls through the images (in single images, such as X-ray and mammography, it pans the image); two fingers spread or pinched = zoom; two fingers dragged together without changing distance = window (horizontal width, vertical level); double tap = enlarges the viewport.
Mammography: the two breasts side by side (or current and prior) are aligned at nipple height. In tomosynthesis, the thickness menu creates thick MIP slabs (useful for calcifications).
Pan and Zoom; right button = zoom, middle button or Shift = pan; mouse wheel or arrows = scroll through the images.

Magnifier (or the L key with any tool): enlarges the area under the mouse without changing the image zoom; dragging adjusts the window; + and − (or Alt + mouse wheel) change the magnification, [ and ] the size; Esc closes it.

Linked point (yellow crosshair icon, or Alt + click with any tool): clicking a finding in one viewport, the other viewports (sagittal, coronal, other series, even the prior exam, which is coregistered automatically) go to the same point and mark it with a yellow crosshair, solid if it is in the displayed slice and dashed if it is nearby; dragging the point moves it; Esc removes it.

Window keys: in CT 1 abdomen, 2 lung, 3 bone, 4 brain, 5 angio, 6 mediastinum, 7 liver, 0 automatic (they can be changed with ⚙ Customize windows and keys); in X-ray 1 bone, 2 soft tissue, 3 high contrast; in mammography (without the layout bar) 1 calcifications, 2 dense breast, 3 skin, 4 high contrast. The key is written next to the item in the window menu. The chosen window applies only to the series of the active viewport. F11: full-screen viewer; Ctrl+J: synchronize the viewports (Ctrl+J again removes it). At opening the exam is always in a single viewport (1×1): layouts are chosen from the buttons. Comparison with the prior: «Compare» places the prior exam side by side, registers it automatically (translation and rotation) and reconstructs it on the plane of the current one, so when scrolling the two exams show the same point even if the patient was positioned differently; «⇄» restores the original images of the prior. In chest CTs with the AI second read the 🫁 button shows the nodules found, circled on the images, with «go» (for students after answering). MPR + 3D opens without 3D (axial, coronal, sagittal): the «3D» button adds it; in brain and neck exams the 3D starts with the vessels only. Brain: at opening the axial series straightens automatically (🧠⟂: midsagittal plane by symmetry, tilt on the anteroposterior axis of the brain; Ax for the original images). «⊞4» compares up to 4 exams, also from different scanners, all registered and reconstructed on the plane of viewport A. The linked point (Alt + click) in the other exams is refined on the area around the point, so it lands on the same structure. «MS» among the layouts: T1 above and FLAIR/STIR below for each brain MRI (up to 8 viewports); «🧠 MS» looks for hyperintense lesions and marks the new ones compared with the prior in red (automatic estimate to be checked).

Rotate 90° (toolbar button; Shift + click counterclockwise) and Flip (H key): for X-rays and ultrasounds acquired crooked; it applies to the active viewport, measurements follow the image; “Reset view” removes them.

Freehand or polygonal ROI (polygon icon): dragging draws freehand, closing on release; with single clicks you place the polygon vertices, which closes with a double click, Enter or by clicking the first point (Backspace removes the last vertex, Esc cancels). It gives the same values as the elliptical ROI (mean, standard deviation, min/max, area; SUV in PET), is copied to the other phases and appears in the density table.

Measurements in the report (sheet-with-checkmark icon, or the I key): the measurements of the active image go into the free-text report where the cursor is, as in PACS: “finding of 14 × 11 mm (image 171)”, “diameter of 9 mm”, “mean density 34 ± 12 HU (ROI of 2.1 cm²)”, “SUVmax 8.2”, angle, Cobb and cardiothoracic ratio. Each press adds the measurements not yet inserted (if they are all already in the report, the last one).
Measurement (mm), elliptical ROI (mean, standard deviation, min/max, area; in CT in HU, in PET in SUV), Angle.
Density profile: you draw a line and a graph of the values along the line appears, with the bands of air, fat, water, tissues and calcium.
Histogram: after each ROI, the distribution of values appears with the percentages of fat, fluid, tissue and calcium/contrast.

Arrow with annotation (T key) and 📸 Key (K key, or B + click on the image): mark the images that justify the answer. Key images appear in the strip below the images (a click on the thumbnail goes back to that image with its window; a caption to write, ✕ to hide it, the number next to 📸 to reopen it) and in the report; they reach the teacher with the answer, with the annotations and the caption. On the platform they cannot be downloaded.

💾 Save annotations (exam or series, or Ctrl+S): measurements, arrows, notes and key images are restored when you reopen the case in this browser; unsaved ones are lost when the case is closed and, if there are any, the platform asks whether to save them. On the scroll bar an “A” marks the images with annotations (yellow if not saved) and a number marks the key images: a click takes you to the image.
Measurement text (distance, RECIST, ROI, angle, arrow, Cobb): drag it with the mouse where it is least in the way, a dashed line links it to the measurement; this also works in the MPR.

RECIST 1.1: a single measurement. Lesion: longest diameter (target if ≥ 10 mm, or twice the slice thickness if it is more than 5 mm); a second click on the RECIST button switches to lymph nodes: short axis (target ≥ 15 mm, 10-14 mm pathological non-target, < 10 mm normal), another click goes back to lesions. At most 5 targets, 2 per organ: you choose them. The sum of diameters goes into the Σ RECIST 1.1 scale with one click.

🤖 Comparison with the prior exam (with a prior exam open): in chest CTs analyzed by the AI, the table of nodules before and after (diameter, volume, doubling time, Lung-RADS growth, RECIST), which in quiz cases is shown after the answer; in the other exams and in the downloadable viewer, “＋ Add lesion” and a click on the lesion in the current exam: the volume is measured automatically, the lesion is found in the other exam and measured there too. These are estimates to be checked on the images; “Copy to report” brings the comparison into the report.
Sharpness: edge contrast filter with three levels; especially useful in X-rays.

Invert, Cine (automatic playback; next to it, the speed in frames per second: “auto” = original speed of ultrasound clips, 12 for the other series, or from 5 to 50), Reset, Clear measurements, Full screen (icon on the right; double click on a viewport to enlarge it).

Semiautomatic volume (cube icon): you click inside the lesion and the platform follows it in the neighboring images (up to 6 cm from the point) and calculates volume, mean density and extent. If the region spills into adjacent tissues a warning appears: click more centrally or use RECIST. For lung nodules on CT the measurement is 3D and dedicated: threshold −400 HU for solid and calcified nodules, −650 HU for ground-glass or part-solid ones; vessels, chest wall, diaphragm and mediastinum attached to the nodule are detached. It is an estimate for training: always check the outline.
Doubling time: by measuring the volume of the same lesion in the current exam and in a prior, the doubling time (and the percentage growth) is shown, calculated from the months between the two exams.

Comparison with the prior (“Δ” button, in cases with multiple CT or MRI exams of the same region): the prior is coregistered to the current exam (translation and rotation, even with the head in a different position), resampled in the same plane as the image and intensity-normalized (MRI has no fixed units). Three views: red/blue on the image (red = new or more intense, for example a new lesion in FLAIR; blue = reduced), difference image, prior in the same plane (scroll and compare at a glance). In CT only soft tissues are compared; edges still give false signals: always check on the images.

McDonald 2017 form (Σ Scales, in MRI with suspected demyelination): sites of dissemination in space (periventricular, cortical/juxtacortical, infratentorial, spinal cord), dissemination in time (enhancing and non-enhancing lesions, new lesion at follow-up, oligoclonal bands), clinical picture, central vein sign and features of vascular disease for the differential diagnosis.

Educational radiomics (“Rad” button): for the elliptical ROIs and volumes drawn, overlaid histogram and side-by-side numbers: mean, standard deviation, percentiles, skewness, kurtosis, entropy and uniformity of the histogram; texture with the co-occurrence matrix (contrast, homogeneity, energy, entropy, correlation). It shows that lesions that look similar to the eye can be different; the values depend on thickness, filter and contrast, so lesions of the same series are compared.

Other AI analyses (in “AI: automatic measurements”, calculated on the Mac at full resolution; for students after answering): intracranial hemorrhage (volume and ABC/2 estimate), ventricles (volume, Evans index, midline shift), right and left pleural effusion and pericardial effusion, lung nodules (second read, with diameter and volume), liver segment volumes with the remnant liver after hepatectomies, liver lesions and renal cysts, body composition at L3 (muscle area, visceral and subcutaneous fat; with height, SMI and sarcopenia). “Trend across exams” puts the same numbers from all follow-ups in a table; findings can also be shown in color and in 3D from the AI menu.

Student reports (Analytics → Reports, for teachers): each written report (in “Report only” or optional) with the automatic comparison against the expected findings (findings not found and incorrect statements). The teacher can give a grade (0-100) and a comment: the student sees them in the case and on their home page. Grade and comment are also in the results CSV.

Anatomy from AI segmentation (CT calculated on the Mac): the “?” tool (What structure is this) gives the name and outline of the structure at the clicked point; the “Anat” button starts the anatomy quiz: the platform asks for a structure, you look for it by scrolling through the images and click it (two attempts, then it is highlighted). For students it is available after answering the case, because the outline of the organs may hint at the finding.

Lesion followed over time: in cases with multiple exams, after the volume of a lesion, “Follow over time” finds it again in the other exams of the same region (it picks the similar series, coregisters the exams and refines the position on the area around the lesion), measures it and shows the graph of maximum diameter and volume over time, with the RECIST 1.1 response (a single target lesion: PR −30% from baseline, PD +20% and at least +5 mm from the nadir) and the volume doubling time. Each automatic measurement is checked with “go”; if it is wrong or the lesion was not found, “redo” or “measure by hand” opens the exam at the expected point: click inside the lesion and the measurement enters the graph.
Thick slab in 2D: the “Slab” menu (5-40 mm) shows MIP, MinIP or the average of several images, useful for nodules, vessels and emphysema.

Calculators: Cobb angle (two lines on the endplates of the end vertebrae), cardiothoracic ratio in X-ray (diameter of the heart and of the chest) and, in head CT, ASPECTS with the 10 regions of the middle cerebral artery.

MPR + 3D: the volume rendering preset is chosen by the type of exam (CT angiography: vessels and bones, with 10 mm MIP in the planes; bone; lung; heart) and can be changed from the menu. There are 25 3D presets, divided into CT (angio, coronaries, heart, organs, bone, lung, air, MIP) and MRI.

Automatic coregistration (icon next to “Align”): with two different studies open in two viewports (for example the CT and the MRI), the active viewport serves as the reference and the platform finds the shift that makes the two volumes most similar (mutual information: it works across different modalities too). If needed, refine with “Align” and the corresponding points.

Fusion: two overlaid series, in 2D and in MPR: PET on CT and, after coregistration, also MRI on CT, MRI on MRI or the follow-up on the prior exam. In the “Below” and “Above” menus you choose the base series and the one to overlay (the plane is indicated next to each series: axial, coronal, sagittal); if the planes differ a warning appears, because the overlay works only on the same plane. With series from different studies, automatic coregistration starts by itself. The overlay appears only in the “Below” viewport. You choose the colormap (16, in groups: nuclear medicine such as hot, hot metal blue, PET, NIH spectrum and thermal; perceptual such as viridis, magma, inferno and plasma; rainbow and jet; single-color, green and magenta for comparing two series), the opacity and the scale; for CT and MRI the transparency follows the signal, so dark areas stay transparent. In the 3D panel, with PET fusion active, the PET alone is shown in color, with the same colormap and the same scale.

MPR + 3D: the MPR views always open on “Thin slab”; thickness and MIP/MinIP are changed from the menu. “Without table”, “Without bone” and “Without rib cage” (CT only) process the volume rendering; without the rib cage, the spine, heart, lungs and thoracic vessels remain. “Segment” automatically extracts, with classical rules: lungs (right and left volume), liver (if it is not captured well: crosshair center in the liver and “Liver from crosshair center”), vessels with contrast (CT angiography and MR angiography), aorta (the whole visible vessel, arch included, even in venous and delayed phase, with the approximate maximum diameter and its position: to be verified with the CPR or the ruler), kidneys (contrast-enhanced CT), bladder, intestinal gas and brain. The structure appears colored in the three views, with its volume, and in 3D the organs appear as a smooth surface; “Remove segmentation” returns the complete 3D. These are educational estimates, not clinical measurements. In the CT for which it has been calculated, “AI segmentation” (TotalSegmentator) also appears: up to 117 structures, in groups (abdominal organs, chest with the lung lobes, vessels, bones with numbered vertebrae and ribs, muscles, brain and spinal cord) or one at a time (for example pancreas, adrenal glands, prostate, portal vein), each with its own color and volume. This too is an automatic estimate to be verified. “AI: automatic measurements” calculates from the AI segmentation the maximum diameter of the thoracic and abdominal aorta (separated at the hiatus, upper margin of T12), volume and craniocaudal length of spleen and kidneys (splenomegaly above 314 cm³ or 13 cm), volume and mean density of the liver with the liver − spleen difference (steatosis criteria valid only without contrast), prostate and pancreas volume.

MPR, measurements: besides distance, ROI (also 3D) and angle there are RECIST 1.1 (also on oblique planes: longest diameter of the lesion and short axis, the one to use for lymph nodes) and Volume (cube icon): you bring the center of the reference lines onto the lesion and press; the semiautomatic volume is calculated on the original series as in 2D. The I key (or the sheet icon) brings into the report the measurements made in the MPR, with the plane (axial, coronal, sagittal, oblique). The large viewport is on the left (axial at opening, with the “Scroll” tool), the other three views in a column on the right: a double click on a small view brings it into the large viewport (and sends the large one to its place); double click on the large view: only that one, full size. Scrolling, zoom, pan and measurements also work in the small views. A measurement is deleted with the eraser (click on the measurement) or by selecting it and pressing Del; the bin, next to the sheet icon, deletes them all. “⊞ Series” creates a series reconstructed from the plane of the large viewport, oblique too (for example to straighten a rotated head, after rotating the reference lines), and opens it in 2D, where it is scrolled and measured like the others; Ax/Cor/Sag return to the standard planes. With the reference lines, a click on a point moves the center there; as in 2D, wheel button up = zoom in and down = zoom out, Shift + drag = pan (also in 3D), right button = window.

CPR (curved reformat): press CPR, click the points along the vessel (or ureter, duct…) in the MPR views, even changing view or slice, then “Create CPR”: the vessel appears “straightened” with the scale in centimeters; the cursor rotates it around the centerline and the menu changes its width.

Vessel analysis: press CPR, click the start and end of the segment (at the center of the vessel, even in different views) and press “Vessel analysis”. The centerline is found automatically inside the vessel; the CPR appears, along with the graph of diameters along the vessel (equivalent, minimum and maximum) and the interpolated reference between the upstream and downstream segments. The narrowest point is marked on the CPR with the stenosis as a % of the diameter (and of the area) and the grade (minimal, mild, moderate, severe, occlusion); “Copy to report” adds the sentence to the report.

Σ Scales and classifications: the panel opens below the images, which remain whole. Available scales: RECIST 1.1 (solid tumor response, in oncologic exams: sum of diameters current, baseline and nadir, non-target lesions and new lesions), RENAL and PADUA (renal masses), Bosniak 2019 with CT and MRI criteria (cystic renal masses), PI-RADS v2.1 (prostate, with prostate volume and PSA density), ACR TI-RADS (thyroid nodules), Fleischner 2017 (incidental lung nodules), Lung-RADS v2022 (lung cancer screening), O-RADS US and MRI (adnexal masses), breast with BI-RADS and ACR density, Couinaud liver segments, LI-RADS v2018 CT/MRI and LR-TR (post-treatment), US LI-RADS, steatosis, AAST 2018 (spleen, liver and kidney trauma), Genant (vertebral fractures: grade 0-3 according to height loss) and Fazekas (white matter hyperintensities, periventricular and deep). Diameters are typed or taken from the last measurement made with the ruler or RECIST (in RECIST 1.1 the current sum is taken with one click from the exam's RECIST measurements); the result, with the category, the recommendation and the data entered, is copied into the report with a click. These are the published versions indicated in each scale. In PI-RADS you click on the drawing of the prostate (v2.1 sector map) the sectors occupied by the lesion; in the “Breast” scale you click on the drawing where the lesion is and you get side, quadrant and clock position, with distance from the nipple, depth, BI-RADS category and ACR density; in the “Liver segments” scale you click on the Couinaud map. If the case asks for a scale, the notice “Σ This case also asks for…” appears in the question panel: you fill in the form and, when the answer is confirmed, the correction shows your form next to the teacher's, item by item (✓ same, ≈ close, ✗ different). The panel shows only the scales suited to the case (by modality and organ); if there are none, the Σ button does not appear. Deauville (lymphoma, FDG PET-CT): uptake of the most avid site compared with the mediastinal blood pool and the liver; the three values are copied from the last ROI with a click (on the PET or on the fusion).

Segmental wall motion of the left ventricle (Σ, echocardiograms and cardiac cases): bull's eye of the 17 AHA segments (anterior at the top, septum on the left, apex at the center). You choose the score on the right (1 normokinesis, 2 hypokinesis, 3 akinesis, 4 dyskinesis, not assessable) and click the segments; the result gives the abnormal segments, the usual coronary territory (left anterior descending, right coronary, circumflex) and the wall motion score index (WMSI, mean of the segments assessed: 1 = normal), with the estimated ejection fraction if entered. Like the other scales, the teacher saves it as the case answer and the student compares it after answering.

PET: the elliptical ROI on the PET (or on the CT with the PET in fusion) gives SUVmax, SUVpeak (mean in 1 cm² around the maximum, in the slice) and SUVmean. The semiautomatic volume (cube icon) clicked on a PET lesion calculates the metabolic volume (MTV, threshold at 41% of SUVmax), SUVmax, SUVmean and TLG (MTV × SUVmean). The phase table with the wash-in and wash-out curves appears only for multiphase CT and dynamic MRI: between CT and PET it makes no sense.

Ultrasound clips: each clip is a series (“clip 1”, “clip 2”…); the ▶ button (cine) plays it at the ultrasound machine's speed (or at the one chosen in the menu next to it), the slider scrolls it frame by frame.

Cardiac measurements (heart icon, only in echocardiograms): you choose the view (apical 4- or 2-chamber LV, 4-chamber RV) and the phase; stop on the end-diastole or end-systole frame and click the endocardium from one side of the annulus to the other passing through the apex (Enter or click on the first point to close, ⌫ removes the last point, Esc starts over). The left ventricle is measured with the disk method (Simpson, 20 disks along the long axis; biplane if both 4- and 2-chamber are present): end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes and ejection fraction, with the ASE/EACVI 2015 normal values. For the right ventricle, end-diastolic and end-systolic areas and fractional area change (FAC, normal ≥ 35%): RV volume is not estimated in 2D. “Copy to report” adds the results to the free-text report. Semiautomatic contour (LV, 4 or 2 chamber): “✳ Semiautomatic contour”, then three clicks (annulus on the septal side, apex, annulus on the opposite side); the program looks for the edge between the dark cavity and the bright wall. In clips, “▶ Track in clip” follows the border in all frames, shows the area curve and automatically places the end-diastole and end-systole tracings (beat with the median EF). It is our own tool, with no trained models: always check the contour and, if it is wrong, retrace it by hand.

Cardiac cines in multiple viewports: in cardiac MRI cases, with the viewports linked (chain button) all cines are set to the same phase of the cycle (proportionally, even if the series have a different number of phases) and ▶ plays them together: for example 4 viewports with 4-chamber, 2-chamber, 3-chamber and short axis. At the top left of each viewport you can read the phase and the time from the R wave.

Cardiac MRI (heart-with-circle icon, in cardiac MRI cases): 1) on a mid-ventricular short-axis slice, click at the center of the left ventricular cavity: the program follows the cavity in all slices and in all phases of the cycle (bright blood in the cines), chooses end-diastole (maximum volume) and end-systole (minimum volume) and calculates volumes, stroke volume, ejection fraction and cardiac output; 2) the same for the right ventricle; in the table, remove the basal slices containing the atrium or the outflow tract; the threshold and the papillary muscle box change the contour; a wrong contour is corrected by hand (Enter closes). 3) LV mass requires the epicardium traced by hand at end-diastole on all included slices (myocardium × 1.05 g/mL). 4) Flow: in the phase-contrast series click the center of the vessel and then the border: peak velocity, forward and backward volumes, regurgitant fraction (venc is read from the sequence name or typed). With height and weight the values are indexed to body surface area. Other measurements: 5) annulus excursion (septal and lateral MAPSE, TAPSE): click on the annulus at end-diastole and on the same point at end-systole; 6) atria: left atrial contour in 4- and 2-chamber (biplane area-length volume, indexed) and right atrial area; 7) late enhancement: on each slice after gadolinium, epicardium, endocardium and a circle in the remote myocardium; myocardium above mean + n SD (2, 3, 5 or 6) is marked in red, with the percentage and grams; T1 and ECV: enter the T1 of myocardium and blood before and after contrast and the hematocrit. “Report template” inserts the cardiac MRI report outline (technique, ventricles, atria, valves, tissue characterization, pericardium, conclusions) already filled in with the measurements made; “Wall motion (Σ)” opens the 17-segment bull's eye. “Copy to report” adds the measurements to the text.

T2* and iron (“More measurements” menu, in MRI cases with multi-echo series): open the mid-ventricular short-axis slice (or a slice of the liver) and draw a ROI in the full-thickness interventricular septum (or in the liver parenchyma, away from vessels). The ROI is carried over automatically to all echoes of the same slice: the panel shows the graph of signal as a function of echo time, the T2* and R2* with two models (with offset, for low T2*, and truncated) and the class: heart > 20 ms normal, 10-20 ms mild-moderate overload, < 10 ms severe; liver with the estimate of iron concentration (LIC, calibration on biopsy by Garbowski 2014). “Copy to report” adds the measurement to the text.

Viewports: from 1 to 8 series together, also with custom layouts (“＋ New layout…” in the menu: drag on the grid, large and small viewports, saved with a name); with Sync, viewports of the same plane follow position and zoom, those on different planes show the reference line. Ctrl + click (⌘ + click on Mac) on a series opens it in a new viewport; the ✕ at the top right of a viewport closes it and the others widen. “▢ 2×1” places two viewports one above the other, for vertical screens.
Align: coregistration of different studies (CT-CT, CT-MRI, MRI-MRI) by clicking the same anatomical point in two viewports.
Automatic alignment (crosshair-with-star icon): with two different studies in two viewports, it aligns the second to the active viewport with a translation; it can be refined with “Align”.
Subtraction: image minus the baseline phase at the same position; only the contrast enhancement remains.
PET fusion: the PET overlaid on the CT, with opacity and scale in SUV, also in MPR.
MPR + 3D: multiplanar reformats, MIP/MinIP with adjustable thickness and volume rendering.

Study tabs: with prior exams, each study has its own tab; with many follow-ups the sequence number appears (1 = the oldest) and, if known, the interval from the first exam (T0, +6 h, +2 d 4 h). The “Compare with prior” button (next to the viewports) places the active exam and the prior side by side in two viewports, even if it concerns another region, with the series of the same type and plane (for example axial T2 with axial T2); the viewports synchronize only if the series are in the same plane and cover the same area. Repeated clicks: ever older exams.
Mammography: keys 1-5 for the layouts (4 views, CC, MLO, comparison with the prior); in tomosynthesis the side indicator shows the slice.
Dynamic phases: the phases of a multiphase CT or MRI on one screen, synchronized.
Collapsible question panel: the ‹ › tab on the left edge of the panel hides it and gives all the space to the images; the choice is kept for the next openings.

Collapsible series bar: a click on “Series ▾” closes it (a thin row remains), another reopens it. With the mouse over the thumbnails, the wheel scrolls the list of series; the title and the exam tabs always stay visible. The mouse instructions are on a single line: the full text appears on hover or with a click. “← Case list” at the top returns to the list.

On the phone the question panel is a bottom sheet: tap or drag the handle (or ▾ ▴) to shrink it, bring it to half height or expand it; the Next and Confirm buttons always stay at the bottom, within thumb reach. After confirming, the sheet expands by itself to show the correction.
The quiz guides the report in order: first the exam technique, then one anatomical region at a time, finally the conclusion. At each step the most useful series may open by itself.

Two ways to answer, chosen at the top of the panel: “☑ Multiple choice” (the statements to select, region by region) and “✍ Report only”, in which you write the report as in the ward without seeing the options. In “report only” mode the score comes from comparing the report with the expected findings (by keywords, recognizing the most common synonyms such as adenopathy/lymph node, hypoattenuating/hypodense, neoplasm/mass, and negations: “no effusion”, “effusion absent” or “no evident rib fractures” count as absence, so an expected finding such as “absence of effusion” must be written negated; incorrect statements written as present remove points, theory ones do not; AI never affects the score); after confirming, the options appear with the correct ones highlighted. The choice is kept for the following cases.

Request and priors: when the teacher has entered them, below the clinical history appear the request (ward, priority, laboratory tests such as creatinine or PSA, allergies, medications, devices, pregnancy) and “🗂 Priors” with the text of the reports of prior exams (“compared with the exam of…”), with a button to open their images when available. Reports written specifically for the exercise are marked.

📞 Communication of the result (box in the last step; if you do not choose, the first «Confirm» reminds you, the second confirms with the report only): you choose whether the result must be communicated besides the report and with what urgency (report is enough, deferred within days, urgent within hours, immediate within minutes), to whom (requester or ward, Emergency department, general practitioner, patient), how (phone with confirmation, tracked message, report only) and what is said; “Log” adds to the report the communication sentence with the time. The time counts from the opening of the case. In cases where the teacher has indicated the expected communication, after the answer the score appears with the individual items; calling when the report was enough removes points.

In the written report: “📋 Report template” inserts an outline by region (chest CT, abdominal CT, brain CT and MRI, prostate MRI with PI-RADS, pelvic MRI with FIGO, mammography with BI-RADS, chest X-ray, PET-CT with Deauville, abdominal ultrasound, generic outline); the Tab key moves to the next “…” field. Uppercase headings and “…” left empty do not count in the automatic evaluation. “🎤 Dictate” writes by voice in Italian only if speech recognition runs on the computer (recent Google Chrome; the audio never goes to the internet, in other browsers dictation stays off): “punto” (period), “virgola” (comma), “due punti” (colon), “a capo” (new line), “nuovo paragrafo” (new paragraph); “14 per 11 millimetri” becomes “14 × 11 mm”. Quality on medical terms must be verified: always reread the text.
More than one answer may be correct, except in the Conclusions, where you choose the most suitable conclusion.
For each answer chosen you indicate how sure you are: Sure, Probable or Hypothesis.
After confirming you see the score by region, the expected report and the discussion; “Show the finding” takes you to the series, the image and the window in which the finding is best seen.

Free-text report: below the answers you can write your own report; after confirming it is compared with the expected findings, by keywords: findings cited, findings missed and distractors written as present. Negative phrases (“no”, “without”, “none”, “absence of”, “rules out”…) are recognized: a negated finding does not count as cited, a negated distractor is not an error. The report reaches the teacher with the answer.

📝 Report editor (in the image toolbar or in the report box): the same editor as the downloadable viewer, with bold, headings and lists, templates, “＋ Insert the measurements”, Σ Scales with the filled-in drawings, key images with their caption and dictation (only if speech is recognized on the computer). “⧉ Separate window” opens it in another window, even on another screen, with the same layout (data on the left, report on the right), while you scroll the images; ⛶ makes it full screen. If the browser blocks pop-up windows, the report is placed next to the images. The text goes back into the “Write your report” box and is sent with the answer. It can be printed or saved as PDF or Word, without the key images.

Question on the figure (📍): before confirming you press “Indicate on the image” and click on the finding in the indicated series. The point is worth 20% of the score: centered, close or missed relative to the teacher's mark, which appears after the correction.
Points, streaks of correct answers and levels count only on the first attempt.

sezioni.titolo: Training by profile: paths, review, exercises
blocchi: Profiles: physicians, radiologic technologists (TSRM), nurses and emergency department. Each sees the paths for their profile, chosen with “Who you are” in the profile; each path has a level and its objectives. Teachers and administrators see all paths and can filter them by profile.

Paths for TSRM: image quality in CT with phantoms, conventional radiology, mammography, protocol selection. For nurses and the emergency department: devices on chest X-ray, urgent findings to recognize.
Wrong acquisitions (TSRM and radiologists): exams to be repeated or corrected because of positioning, centering, motion, artifacts or protocol.
Ward misses: cases arising from real errors, anonymized, with the lesson to be drawn after the answer.
Error review: a case you got wrong comes back after 1, 7 and 30 days until you solve it (3 correct answers in a row).
Custom path: after 10 cases it shows the topics you get wrong most often (for example the lung bases in abdominal CT) and suggests cases chosen for the purpose.

Find the error: on a case you have already completed, a report with a wrong sentence to find and correct, or with a missing finding to choose. Results are saved in your history and your teacher sees them in the monthly summary.

🧾 Justification and protocol (among the paths, or from the address #/esame/protocollo): an exam request arrives with ward, priority, clinical question, clinical information, laboratory (creatinine, eGFR…), allergies, devices and pregnancy. You decide whether it is appropriate, which exam to perform, whether with contrast, which phases and which precautions (hydration, metformin, previous reactions, hyperthyroidism, pacemaker, pregnancy). Immediate correction with the explanation and the reference guideline; the score stays in the browser.
Entry test and final test: in paths with at least 6 cases, 5 timed cases before starting and the same ones at the end, to measure improvement.
Certificates: for each completed path and for each level exam passed (at least 60%), with date, score and verification code, to print or save as PDF.
Theory cards: after the answer, signs to look for, classifications and pitfalls of the case topic.

Simulated on-call shift (⏱ Mock exam → “On-call shift”): 8 or 10 mixed urgent cases (urgent findings, emergency department, trauma) in random order, only with emergency department modalities (X-ray, CT, ultrasound) or also MRI if the wards are reported, a single time for the entire shift (45, 60 or 90 minutes) and written report only. The teacher rereads the reports and marks the discrepancy for each case: none, minor or major (changes patient management). Your shifts, with the discrepancies, are on the same page.

Simulated worklist (⏱ Mock exam → “Worklist”): 6-12 requests as in a real reporting session, in three separate scenarios: emergency department (X-ray, CT, ultrasound), ward (X-ray, CT, ultrasound, MRI) and nuclear medicine (separate list, never mixed with the other modalities). Each request has origin, priority (🔴 urgent, 🟠 high, ⚪ routine), clinical question and expected reading time per modality. You choose the order from the list (urgent ones first); some requests arrive while you work. Written report only; reading time is measured for each case. At the end: score, time compared with expected, urgent cases reported; the teacher rereads the reports and marks the discrepancies as in the on-call shift.

Comparison with colleagues (home page, progress box): for each modality in which you have completed at least 3 cases, your average score, the sensitivity (findings present that you indicated) and the specificity (incorrect statements that you avoided), with the colleagues' median and your percentile. It is anonymous and appears only with at least 5 colleagues in the same modality; first attempts at multiple-choice cases count.
Case outcome: where the teacher knows it, after the answer how it turned out appears (histology, follow-up or surgery).

Suggest a case (home page, progress box): you upload an exam from your computer, anonymized in the browser as in the “New case” page, with title, clinical suspicion, history and a description for the teacher. A declaration that you are entitled to share it is required, with the authorization of the institution. An author teacher checks images and anonymity, writes findings and questions and publishes it, or explains why it is not published; the status of your suggestions is on the same page. A maximum of 5 pending suggestions per person.

🏁 Challenges between friends (menu «Challenges» or «Training» → «Challenge your friends»): pick 3 to 10 cases, give a title and share the link (WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Facebook, X, email or copy). You tag your friends in the post: the site never posts for you. Whoever opens the link sees the challenge, signs in or signs up (also with Google or LinkedIn) and accepts it. Cases are solved as in the mock exam: corrections are shown at the end. The first answer to each case after accepting is the one that counts. Optional leaderboard with the name you choose: average score on the challenge cases, then time. It closes at the chosen deadline or after 90 days; whoever created it can close it earlier.

For teachers: double reading. In Analytics → Reports, “Annotate on the images” opens the case: draw arrows with annotation and measurements, then “Save to review”; the student finds them in the case with “Show teacher's annotations”.

Monthly summary (Analytics → Monthly, and on the first Monday of the month also by email): who has been inactive for 30 days, the topics most often wrong, cases that are too easy or too difficult with the most frequently chosen distractor, entry and final tests.
In the case editor: “Case from a real error” with the lesson, “Wrong acquisition” and the linked theory cards.

On-call shifts and worklists: in Analytics → Reports, for each report choose the discrepancy (none, minor, major) along with the grade and the comment; in Analytics → Exams the “Simulated on-call shifts” table counts for each shift the major and minor discrepancies and the reports still to be reviewed.

You become a teacher by checking “I am also a teacher” at registration or from the profile, with “Become a teacher”: it is immediate. You see only the registered users who choose you as reference. The Manage menu collects all the functions.

Email notifications: when someone chooses you as teacher you receive a message; every Monday morning the weekly summary arrives (cases completed and score of each person, who has been inactive, assignments due). They can be turned off from the profile, along with the other notifications.

My students: the list of those who chose you as reference teacher (category, year, site, cases completed), even before they have answered a case; then the detail with average score, trend, confidence calibration, weak areas and cases completed.

Classes and assignments: you create a class with those who chose you, and add assignments (cases chosen by hand or from a path) with a due date. With “Notify by email” the registered users receive the notice; two days before the due date a reminder goes to those who have not finished. If a user removes you from their teachers, they leave your classes.

Teaching paths (Manage → Teaching paths): you create a sequence of cases to be done in order, with title and description; you choose them from a list, from another path or with “Copy and edit” from a site path, and reorder them with the arrows. The path appears on the home page of those who chose you as teacher, before the site ones, with progress and certificate. The administrator can make it visible to everyone. Draft cases stay hidden from students until they become visible.

Results and analytics: for each case the difficulty, the discrimination of each option, the secondary findings missed, the score by region and the key images indicated (with the student's caption and notes: “👁 Open” reopens the case on that image, with the same window and zoom; the same images appear under each report in Analytics → Reports); the Error map shows in which regions errors are most frequent and which distractors mislead; the “Most frequently missed findings” table lists, case by case, the findings not reported and in what fraction of the answers. The class filter limits all statistics to the members of a class. The CSV downloads all the data of your registered users.

Case difficulty: in the list, teachers also see the average score and the number of answers for each case; if the calculated difficulty differs from the one indicated in the editor, an indication appears.

Case management: summary (visible, drafts, cases with checks to do), filters by status, modality and region, sorting by clicking the columns; for each case answers and average score and the completeness checks (main finding, sections without a correct answer, Conclusions, explanation, notes to verify). Actions on multiple cases: make visible, set to draft, export the list, delete (with confirmation).

Case images (Edit case): “View / remove” shows the thumbnails of a series and the large image; you select the images (Shift for a range) or the whole series to remove. “Add images” opens the guided upload (anonymization in the browser) and adds new series to the case. “Download the study” saves all the anonymized images in a .zip. “Intervals between exams” reads from the original folder the date and time of the studies and saves only the interval from the first exam. Changes made on the site are picked up on the Mac at the next publication (removed images end up in the case's “_rimosse” folder).

Case scales: in the open case, Σ panel, you fill in the suitable scale and press “Save as case answer” (only the scales that make sense for that case); at the top of the panel the scales already saved are listed, and a click reopens them for editing. If the calculated result is not the intended one, “✎ Correct or enter the result by hand” lets you write the category and text (“↺ Back to calculation” undoes the change). Students see which scales are asked and, after the answer, the comparison with the teacher's form. “Remove from case” removes it.

Analytics → “Exams”: the level exams of those who chose you, by student and level (first, last, best, trend), with CSV export. The score is recalculated by the server from the answers saved during the test.

Suggestions from registered users (Manage → Draft review, group “Suggestions from registered users”, author teachers only): who suggests and their description. “🔍 Check anonymity” reads the header of all files (it must contain only the technical fields left by the anonymization, the case code and no name, date, facility, physician or private field) and looks for burned-in text in the images (all of them in short series; first, middle and last in long ones), showing the previews with suspicious areas in red. If the headers are anonymous, you look at the previews, confirm and log the check: only then does “Confirm and publish” become active (even from the editor the case does not become visible without the check; if images are added the check must be redone). “I'll correct it” to write findings and questions. “Do not publish” asks for a reason, which the person who suggested it sees; the case stays in draft and can be deleted.
Case outcome (editor, “Teaching use”): type (histology, follow-up, surgery) and text; the student sees it only after the answer.

Staged case (editor, regions): next to the series of a region, check “revealed here”: that series stays closed until the student reaches that question (for example first the PA X-ray, then the lateral, then the CT). In “Teaching use” you add the “Rule to remember” (one line) and “The same sign in other cases” (one line per case: “caso-120 | cavitary lesion with air-fluid level”): the student sees them after the answer, with links to published cases only.

In the case editor, three optional blocks: “Clinical request” (ward, priority ED/inpatient/classes U-B-D-P, laboratory one item per line, allergies, medications, devices, pregnancy), “Prior reports” (date, exam, text, image series, check if the text is written for the exercise) and “Communication of the result” (expected and acceptable urgency, recipients, message keywords, explanation for the student).
Manage → Cases: list of all cases with filter, multiple selection, “Make visible” and “Set to draft”; from each row you open the case or the editor.

Manage → New case: you choose the exam folder; the images are anonymized in the browser and only then uploaded. Summary screens, structured reports and “for processing” images are excluded. The platform also looks for burned-in text in the images (rows of white characters, such as overlaid names and dates) and highlights it in red in the previews: by default the areas are covered in the pixels before sending; you can indicate that they are only markers or exclude the series. Before uploading you must confirm that you have looked at the previews. With multiple regions you can create one case per region.

Case editor: title (only exam and clinical suspicion, for example “Mammography: screening”: never the diagnosis or the ACR density, which the student must derive from the images), clinical suspicion, history, sections of the guided report (with templates: total-body CT, polytrauma, chest X-ray, mammography…), options (main finding, secondary or distractor) with note, discussion, hidden series and viewport layout. “Set the finding view” saves series, image, window and a mark on the finding (the last ROI drawn). With “Question on the figure” the student must indicate the finding with a click, compared with that mark.

Manage → Registered users and teachers: a search and pill filters with the number of people (all, members, teachers, administrators, without a teacher, emails to confirm, never a case, deactivated); then category and “Students of…” a teacher. Each person's actions (role, access, deactivate, delete) are in the ⋯ menu at the end of the row, grouped; “Delete” asks for a second press; sorting by clicking the columns; “CSV” downloads the filtered list (it contains personal data: internal use only). For each account: how they sign in (password or code), activity (cases completed, answers, average first-attempt score, last case), for teachers the students and classes. With ✎ next to a user's teachers you choose their reference teachers: the user and the teacher receive an email and the user can remove them from the profile. You can also activate a registration by hand, deactivate or delete an account, remove the teacher function or make the user an author.

AI segmentation: on the Mac, “~/.radioquiz-ia/venv/bin/python strumenti/segmenta_ia.py caso-NNN” (or --tutti for all cases with CT not yet done) calculates with TotalSegmentator the structures of the already anonymized CT, in 10-30 seconds per series; the result (only labels and geometry, no patient data) goes online with the next publication. In Manage → Cases the checkbox “AI segmentation enabled for everyone” turns it on or off for the whole site; in the case editor the “AI segmentation” checkbox hides it in that case.

Features for students, case by case (administrator only, in the case editor): “Anatomical part recognition” (“?” tool, “Anat” quiz, numbered vertebrae), “Multiple answers” (without the check the student answers only by writing the report, corrected by keywords) and “Score filling” (Σ panel). Authors always see everything; other authors cannot change these checkboxes.
Ultrasound clips: they are imported from the .zip archive (not from the browser); each clip is split into frames (at most 80) and the text outside the image is blacked out in each one.

Manage → “Draft review”: drafts and visible cases with a doubt, grouped, with what to check (the “TO CHECK” block of the note), the expected findings and the buttons “Open with images”, “I'll correct it” and “Confirm and publish”.

Manage → Usage statistics: registered users, active, cases completed, reports, paths completed, exams and monthly trend, in aggregate form only (categories under 3 people merged), to print or save as PDF. They also include reading accuracy by modality (score medians, sensitivity and specificity, only with at least 5 people) and the average improvement between entry and final tests of the paths.

Before every publication, pubblica.command runs the regression tests (cloud/test: security, correction, paths, exams, error-free pages, an answered case, MPR/3D, phone) and the AI segmentation checks (strumenti/controlla_ia.py: geometry, orientation, implausible results). If a test fails it does not publish; wrong segmentations are marked “discarded” and the site does not use them.

Invitations (Manage → Registered users and teachers, “＋ Invite a person” button): name, email and the role card (resident, teacher, administrator), then “Send invitation”. The person receives an email with the link to choose the password (valid for 7 days, one time only); until they choose it, the account is “invitation pending” and you can use “Resend invitation”.

Institution platform (separate installation): no open registration; accounts are created by the institution's administrator with invitations and the roles are decided by them; it starts with no cases, which the institution uploads from Manage → New case (images anonymized in the browser before upload). The site's learning paths are present as empty templates: in Manage → Teaching paths the administrator fills them with their own cases (“Fill with cases” / “Customize”), changes their title and description, hides or restores them; students see only the paths with at least one case. Teachers can still create their own paths. The data controller is the institution.
Whitelist anonymization: only the technical image data remain; identifiers are regenerated.
Images open only after login and only for open cases; hidden series and drafts stay closed to students.
Correct answers never reach the browser before confirmation.

Data are on servers in Italy (AWS, Milan), with backup copies of cases and results: retained file versions, database restore to any point in the last 35 days and a compressed daily copy of the database (answers, results, classes and forms), kept for 90 days.

To open cases you have already seen faster, the browser keeps a copy of their (anonymous) images in the site's private storage, up to 2 GB; clear the site data in the browser to remove it. Answers and personal data are not stored there.
Data controller: Ing. Salvatore Paolo Buemi. Contact for any request about personal data: privacy@radio-quiz.it.

Which data: first and last name, email, professional category, site and year of study (optional), chosen teachers, answers to cases with the times and tools used, date of last login. The password is stored only as an encrypted hash. We do not process users' health data: the case images are anonymous and contain no patient or healthcare facility data.

Why and on what basis: to provide the service requested with registration (art. 6.1.b GDPR): account, cases, progress, sharing of results with the teachers you choose, service emails (confirmation, new password, assignments and reminders; the latter can be turned off from the profile). For platform security and anonymous case statistics (legitimate interest, art. 6.1.f).
Who sees them: you; the teachers you have chosen (results and progress); the service administrators. Data are not sold or used for advertising.

Where: on Amazon Web Services servers in the Milan region (Italy); emails are sent from Amazon SES. Amazon acts as data processor under its own data protection terms; the CloudFront distribution network may serve pages from nodes outside the European Union, covered by the standard contractual clauses.

Google or LinkedIn sign-in (optional): if you choose “Continue with Google” or “Continue with LinkedIn”, the provider identifies you and sends us only your account identifier, your verified email and your name; we do not receive your password or any other account data (contacts, posts, photos), we never post anything on your behalf, and the page contains no Google or LinkedIn code. The provider thus learns that you used your account to sign in to radio-quiz.it, under its own privacy policy (policies.google.com/privacy, linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy). You can always sign in with email and password as well.

Challenges between friends (optional): whoever creates a challenge chooses the title, the cases and an optional deadline; the link can circulate freely and anyone who opens it sees the title, the exams (without diagnosis) and the number of participants, never their names. If you accept a challenge we keep the name you choose (a nickname is fine), the date you joined and whether you want to appear in the leaderboard. You appear in the leaderboard only if you choose to: whoever has the link sees the chosen name, the cases done, the average score and the time, never your answers. You can change your mind or leave the challenge at any time; deleting your account removes you from all leaderboards. Challenges close at the deadline or after 90 days.

Artificial intelligence models in the browser: report correction (optional, started only with a click) downloads the open source Qwen3-4B model from Hugging Face and a library from GitHub the first time. At that moment these services, as when visiting any website, receive the IP address and technical data of the browser; they do not receive the report or any other platform data, because the model runs on the user's computer. The model for the second reading of lung nodules is downloaded from radio-quiz.it instead.

For how long: as long as the account is in use. Accounts inactive for 24 months are deleted, with an email notice one month before; registrations not confirmed after one week. With deletion, the answers to cases remain only in anonymous form, for case statistics.

Your rights: access, rectification, erasure, restriction, objection and portability (articles 15-22 GDPR). From the profile you can correct your data, download them as a file and delete the account; for anything else write to privacy@radio-quiz.it. You can lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (www.garanteprivacy.it).

Cookies: technical only, necessary for operation (login session and access to the case images); some preferences (light or dark theme) also remain in the browser. No profiling cookies or third-party tracking tools, so consent is not needed. To size the service the platform counts pages opened and logins only as daily totals (for example “120 case list pages on November 5”), without linking them to the person.
Registration is restricted to people aged 18 or over.

Radiology Quiz is a proof of concept (POC): a demonstration and experimental training service, free and open to all adults, that shows the platform offered to healthcare institutions and residency programs. It is provided as is, with no guarantee of availability or continuity.

Cases are for training only: they are not diagnostic or therapeutic indications and do not replace clinical judgment. Questions and answers are prepared with care but may contain inaccuracies: report them to privacy@radio-quiz.it or to your teacher.

Teaching content (questions, options, explanations and learning paths) is prepared with the support of artificial intelligence tools and checked by a physician before publication. During use, AI intervenes only where indicated (report correction, nodule detection) and never contributes to the score.

Content may be incomplete, inaccurate or out of date and is provided without warranties. For clinical decisions, the guidelines of scientific societies (for example SIRM, ESR, ACR) and the primary literature prevail.

The downloadable viewer is a training and education tool: it is not a medical device under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and must not be used for diagnosis, clinical reporting or treatment decisions. It does not connect to hospital systems (PACS). The data of the exams opened stay on the user's computer, and the user is responsible for them.
Images are anonymous. It is forbidden to attempt to trace the identity of patients, to mass-download the images or to distribute them outside the platform.
The account is personal: do not share your password. Those who declare themselves teachers see only the data of those who choose them and use it only for training.
We may suspend accounts used improperly. The service may change or be interrupted; the updated terms are always on this page.
To the extent permitted by law, the author is not liable for damages arising from the use of the information outside training.
Anyone who believes that content infringes their rights (for example copyright) can write to info@radio-quiz.it: the content will be checked and, if necessary, corrected or removed.
